articles.title: Tata Motors raises Iveco takeover offer price to 14.40 euro per share
No higher bid: Tata Motors’ final price faces crucial test as Iveco shareholders hold the key

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors raised its all‑cash tender offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion (33.47 % premium to the July 17 2025 price and 6.77 % premium to the July 29 2025 price). The increase is funded via an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank and the company said the price will not be increased further. The offer covers 271.2 million Iveco shares and the acceptance period runs from 7 September to 26 October 2026.

Tata Motors’ €3.91‑billion “best and final” bid for Iveco faces its decisive test as shareholders decide whether to tender enough shares to meet an 80 % threshold (potentially lowered from 95 %). Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, has pledged its 27.06 % stake (43 % voting rights). Minority investors – Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers – together hold about 20 % of Iveco and their participation will be critical. Analysts comment on the strategic impact of a failed deal for both Tata Motors and Iveco.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product collaboration. Tata will provide Stellantis access to its product technology and vehicle architecture; Stellantis will apply its engineering capabilities to develop vehicles for more than 50 global markets. Production will occur in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Ltd (FIAPL), the 50:50 JV between Tata and Stellantis.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have formalised an expanded partnership through a definitive agreement. The deal combines Tata’s vehicle architecture and technology with Stellantis’ global product‑development expertise to create vehicles in India for over 50 markets, with manufacturing at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture. The collaboration is positioned to strengthen India’s role in the global automotive production network and support Stellantis’s portfolio of 14 brands worldwide.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share (a 2 % increase) on 9 October after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the original price. The revised price is described as the “best and final” offer. Three investors – Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers – together hold about 20.4 % of Iveco’s shares and have not tendered, putting the deal at risk before the 26 October deadline. Tata expects the transaction to close by November and notes that Exor’s 27.06 % stake carries 43 % of voting rights.

key_points.text: Tata Motors raised its all‑cash takeover offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the deal at €3.91 billion, representing a 33.47 % premium to the July 17 2025 price and a 6.77 % premium to the July 29 2025 price; the increase is funded by an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank and will not be increased further.

Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion bid is now in its final phase; Exor, holding 27.06 % of Iveco’s common shares (43 % voting rights), has committed its stake, while minority shareholders (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) together hold about 20 % and their tender decisions will determine whether the 80 % acceptance threshold can be met.

Tata Motors’ revised offer, described as its “best and final” price of €14.40 per share, was raised by 2 % on 9 October after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the original offer; three investors holding roughly 20.4 % of Iveco’s shares have not yet tendered, putting the transaction at risk ahead of the 26 October deadline, with the company expecting the deal to close by November.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership to jointly develop vehicle technology and architecture, giving Stellantis access to Tata’s product tech and using Stellantis’ engineering to create vehicles for more than 50 global markets, with manufacturing to be done in India at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture.

The expanded Tata‑Stellantis partnership aims to leverage India’s engineering and manufacturing capacity to produce vehicles for export, supporting Stellantis’s global brand portfolio across Europe, North America, South America, Middle East, Africa and Asia‑Pacific.

industry_context.text: Analysts note that if the Iveco acquisition fails, Iveco would need to fund Europe’s costly transition to cleaner commercial vehicles without the financial backing of a larger parent, highlighting the pressure on European commercial‑vehicle makers to invest in cleaner technologies.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors needs support from silent shareholders owning about 27% of Iveco common shares to reach the 80% acceptance threshold for its €3.9 billion acquisition, after raising the offer to €14.40 per share; about 52.9% of shares have backed the deal so far.

Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 results, projecting revenue growth of around 44‑45% YoY to Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore and adjusted PAT up to 44.3% YoY, driven by ~43% YoY volume expansion; margins are expected to stay under pressure.

Tata Motors became India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in April‑Sept FY27, dispatching over 3.9 lakh units (+43%) and seeing utility‑vehicle dispatches surge 59%; the overall passenger‑vehicle market grew 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units.

Iveco shareholders approved Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion takeover proposals, lowering the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80% and authorising delisting, board appointments and a post‑offer demerger; the tender offer is set to close on Oct 26.

Iveco shareholders approved Tata Motors’ takeover bid, cutting the acceptance threshold to 80 % and raising the offer price to €14.40 per share, valuing the deal at around €3.8 billion, with plans for delisting and restructuring.

key_points.text: Tata Motors must persuade silent shareholders owning about 27% of Iveco common shares to reach the 80% acceptance threshold for its €3.9 billion acquisition, after sweetening the offer to €14.40 per share.

Iveco shareholders approved the takeover proposals, reducing the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%, enabling Tata Motors to proceed with its €3.91 billion acquisition and allowing a post‑offer demerger and delisting.
Tata Motors raised its offer price for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at approximately €3.91 billion.

Analysts expect Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 revenue to grow 43.6%–45.4% YoY to Rs 24,218.4–24,638.1 crore and adjusted PAT to rise up to 44.3% YoY, driven by roughly 43% YoY volume expansion; margins are forecast to remain under pressure.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra to become the second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in India for April‑Sept FY27, with domestic dispatches of over 3.9 lakh units (+43%) and a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle dispatches.

industry_context.text: The Indian passenger‑vehicle industry recorded a 28.3% increase in domestic dispatches to around 26.4 lakh units in April‑Sept FY27.
